severity_scale.factual_blocker: A sentence the records contradict. It blocks leaving that sentence unchanged. No result or count changes.

findings.title: The main text places the buyer's estate reasoning before the omission-framed reply in G13
findings.passage: The buyer already considers that estate logic before the omission-framed reply.
evidence: G13 d251 (Opus counter at $130), returned explanation: "That payment also keeps p4 solvent enough to cover Short Line rent to p2, which matters for how the game continues." This is solvency reasoning. It does not weigh who inherits the yellows.
G13 d252 is Grok's omission-framed reply.

G13 d253 (Opus acceptance), returned explanation: "if player 4 goes bankrupt to player 2, player 2 would inherit the yellows plus Pennsylvania" and "If grok goes bankrupt to me instead, that could hand me the yellows". The estate weighing is recorded here, after the reply.

The casebook in the same package states it correctly: "Its solvency reasoning already appears in the $130 counter, after Grok's opening appeal and before the omission-framed reply." (integrated/sections/casebook.tex, Incident 5).
Source: saved_games/railway-research-8-games-2026-10-26/game-13-185turns-581702d9/run/decisions.jsonl, decisions 250 to 253, read directly.
findings.why_it_matters: The sentence supports the scope statement that the omission cannot be credited with the extra $70. The correct chronology supports the same statement, so only the sentence changes.
findings.check_status: checked against raw records in this review
findings.does_not_change: The incident, its quotations, and the conclusion that the omission's effect is not identified.

findings.title: G12 d249 is described as not an omitted-resource case, and two of its channels first count only the listed sale target
findings.passage: The third payable declaration, G12 Grok d249, is not an omitted-resource case. Grok's note recognizes a sale-based route and its assistant content names a sale, while its received tool call declares.
evidence: First menu at G12 d249 lists one sale target, VIRGINIA_AVENUE, and no mortgage. Holdings are St. Charles 2, States 2, Virginia 3 houses. Cash $43, debt $250.

Returned explanation, in order: "I can only sell houses on Virginia Avenue." "Selling all three houses on Virginia Avenue would raise $150. That leaves a $57 shortfall after paying the $250 rent." "I cannot raise enough cash to cover the rent. I will declare bankruptcy." Then: "I can raise enough cash by selling houses on St Charles Place and States Avenue too. Together with Virginia Avenue, that yields $393 total."

The private note inside the received declare call opens "Full even liquidation cannot cover the $250." It ends "The sell_houses call was the correct action. Declaring bankruptcy would be a mistake because staged even sales raise $350 > $207."
Assistant content names sell_houses_or_hotel with Virginia Avenue, count 2. The public message of the received call is "Bankruptcy. The pinks go with the rest."

The package retains one quotation for this note (transcript_quotes.tex, g12_d249_private_final), which is its last three sentences. The compiled paper displays no quotation for this case and paraphrases only that ending.
The supplement's own rule for the sixteen: "Channel selection must not hide a qualification in another field."
findings.why_it_matters: The paper separates false budgets from conflicting responses. This response contains both a provisional count of listed resources with a bankruptcy conclusion and a later correct route. Saying it is not an omitted-resource case, and reporting only the end of the note, hides the first part. The classification as a text and call conflict survives, because the last stated assessment in every channel is a sufficient route.
findings.check_status: checked against raw records in this review
findings.does_not_change: The count of three payable declarations, the inherited five-house witness, and the distinction between the two failures and this case.

findings.title: The main text names decisions to stop as informative and gives no population for them
findings.passage: The more discriminating observations are their financial inventories, decisions to stop, selected assets and agreement between text and calls. [...] Six above-bound episodes start financing rather than declaring immediately.
evidence: Recomputed from raw decisions: 56 episodes have U* < D. Eight first menus offer only bankruptcy. Of the other 48 first calls, 42 declare and 6 start financing. Of 132 episodes with U* >= D, 129 start financing and 3 declare.
The only place these counts appear is Table 13 in Appendix D, introduced as context for the departures.
final_review/fable_5_2/checks/finance_checks.json, keys first_actions and first_menu_declare_by_region_model.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader of the main text cannot tell whether six is most or few. One sentence gives the denominator. It does not make the table a headline or an accuracy score, and the appendix caption already states why it is not one.
findings.check_status: checked against raw records in this review
findings.does_not_change: The decision not to headline 3/132 against 50/56.

findings.title: The 28 of 30 paragraph says preference, and the mortgage action is always listed first
findings.passage: Asset selection shows a consistent preference in one defined population. [...] These choices preserve development when mortgages already provide sufficient financing.
evidence: Count confirmed: 62 class members, 30 building owners, 28 without any sale. Membership equals integrated/data/development_preservation.json. The two sellers are Opus G12 d282 and G18 d372, one States Avenue house each.

In all 61 first menus that offer both actions, available_actions is [mortgage_property, sell_houses_or_hotel, declare_bankruptcy]. The options object also lists mortgageable keys before sellable keys.
A building sale is offered in 29 of the 30 first menus. One building owner had no sale option.
Nineteen of the 30 payments take one action.

The two Opus exceptions have only railroads listed as mortgageable. Their returned explanations compare a railroad mortgage with a house sale: G12 d282 "mortgaging a railroad would give $100, while selling a house, like one on States Avenue, would only net $50 and drop the rent tier"; G18 d372 "mortgaging one of my three railroads gets $100 but lowers RR rent for the others".
The paper cites yan2026menu for the point that menu presentation can affect execution, and says these records do not identify a menu effect.
findings.why_it_matters: The count is right and the finding is worth keeping. The word preference attributes it to the agents, and the paper's own related work says order can matter. Stating the order and the 29 keeps the paragraph descriptive.
findings.check_status: checked against raw records in this review
findings.does_not_change: The 28 of 30 count, its place in the abstract, or the G13 selective route.

findings.title: The assessment the abstract asks about is on record in 37 first responses, and the paper reports sixteen
findings.passage: In 43 of the 48 responses, at least one readable channel contains a numeral equal to $U_*$, the total asset proceeds $U_*-C$, or the remaining deficit $D-U_*$.
evidence: Split of the 48 by whether buildings lock further mortgages (listed total below full bound): 27 unlocked with 27 matches, 21 locked with 16 matches. None of the 8 forced menus has locked collateral.

I read all 21 locked contexts. In each of the 16 matches the text itemizes the released mortgages. Examples: Grok G3 d601 "After that, pink mortgages are only $70+$70+$80=$220. Total raisable $147+$250+$220=$617"; Gemini G11 d225 "Selling all 5 Red houses ($375) and mortgaging all three Red properties ($340) would only raise $715"; Opus G3 d240 "It seems mortgaging the yellows requires selling Marvin's h[ouse]".

Two itemize released mortgages without a total: Opus G2 d215 ("mortgaging the light-blue properties themselves for $160 once the houses are gone"), Sol G10 d188 ("even subsequently mortgaging light blues adds only $160").
Three state the listed total as a maximum: Sol G3 d426 "maximum $914" (U* 1,074); Opus G5 d309 "only gets me to 639 total" (U* 799); Grok G8 d280 "total $386. No unmortgaged properties." (U* 666).

With the sixteen payable necessity episodes: 37 episodes have U0 < D and M* > M0. 32 first responses count or raise the locked collateral (14 + 16 + 2). Five give a listed-only maximum (Sol twice; Gemini, Opus, Grok once each).
The 121 entries with M* > M0 are 16 + 53 + 30 + 21 + G7. In the 84 outside the 37, U0 >= D.
final_review/fable_5_2/checks/totals_checks.json holds every context. integrated/data/stated_totals_check.json holds the numeral matches.
findings.why_it_matters: The abstract's first question is how agents assess resources that become usable after an action. The supplement's 43 of 48 mixes 27 cases with nothing locked and 21 where the question applies, and the split is where the information is. The 37 episodes more than double the evidence, come from all four configurations, and give the two failures a denominator. The decision log declines 5/37 because 37 is not every entry with unlisted collateral. That is right about the label and leaves the defined population untouched.
findings.proposed_change: R5 in replacement_prose.tex (one supplement paragraph pair and three main-text sentences)
findings.check_status: numeral matches reproduced from the shipped file; the 21 contexts read in this review; the reading is model-assisted
findings.does_not_change: The supplement-only status and narrow wording of 43 of 48. The abstract.

findings.title: The Arena comparison overstates that study's human check
findings.passage: Unlike commerce work classifying a full message corpus with a human annotation check~\cite{li2026arena}, our semantic counts and selected conduct remain model-assisted observations.
evidence: arXiv 2608.14825 abstract page, fetched 15 November 2026: 2,583 emails, a primary classifier, replication with judges from two other model families. The abstract page mentions no human annotation.

My 14 November reading of the HTML (paper_review_2026-11-14/reviews/fable_5_2/literature_matrix.md): a 50-email set labeled by one person who also wrote the codebook, described by the authors as codebook consistency.
The fresh adversarial review reaches the same reading: "a 50-email author-label consistency check, while the full pipeline is model-assisted".
findings.why_it_matters: The sentence sets a human-checked study against this one. Both rely on model readers. The accurate contrast is population coverage and cross-family judges.
findings.check_status: abstract checked now; Appendix A reading inherited from 14 November
findings.does_not_change: The citation or the paragraph's point.

findings.title: Release package: stale sources ship, one recheck is not byte-stable, and the entry point is not yet at any commit
evidence: release_manifest.json lists 101 files. Eleven section files are not read by the build: finance, conduct, negotiation, study, interpretation, scientific_introduction, supplement, necessary_texts, opening_complete, proposer_rows (byte-identical to the 12 November package) and sixteen_full. finance.tex contains "before choosing whether to proceed", "reproducible result" and "survives ten actions"; scientific_introduction.tex contains "negative only when pooled". The 14 November review withdrew all four.

I ran the five README recheck scripts on a copy in my folder. All exit 0. 85 of 86 files come out byte-identical. data/continuation_premises.json differs in key order (32 lines) because refresh_records.py line 68 builds a set of group names and line 71 iterates it. Content is equal. A user who reruns the README command changes that file's hash, and package_release.py --verify then fails.
The five recheck scripts overwrite files inside the package. The README says they read stored records and perform arithmetic.

A static build in another directory gives 29 pages and identical extracted text, and a PDF that differs in 60 bytes near the trailer. The published hash identifies the shipped file and cannot be reproduced elsewhere.

qa/portability.json records an earlier archive (e8139549…, 28 pages). During this review another process regenerated the unpinned release.zip, release.sha256, release_manifest.json and wrote qa/portability_candidate.json at 00:15. That newer record agrees with my build: 29 pages, identical text, 101 packaged files, and a rebuilt PDF hash (4eabfddd…) that differs from the pinned one. The stale qa/portability.json is still in the folder, and the regenerated manifest still lists the eleven unused section files.
git status: docs/research_raw/paper_finalization_2026-11-14/ is untracked at HEAD 863f8ef7. The entry-point path exists at no commit. The decision log records this as M-03 in progress.
README.md line 1 reads "Integrated manuscript — finalization in progress".
PDF Info has empty Title and Author.
findings.why_it_matters: The science is unaffected. A reader who opens the sources finds withdrawn claims in files that look current, and a reader who follows the README can break the hash check.
findings.proposed_change: The five items under "Release changes that are not prose" in replacement_prose.tex
findings.check_status: checked in this review; the commit and archive are the owner's to make
findings.does_not_change: Any number or sentence in the paper, apart from naming the commit in Appendix I.
